transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 09:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (CTO, StratusLedger), Priya Nair (Netops), Jordan Lee (Platform)

Auto-summary (brief):
- Pilot steady but two AZs showing intermittent p95 latency spikes during peak synthetic load; likely egress shaping + MTU mismatch suspected.
- Telemetry pipeline into Splunk drops some flow logs; sampling config needs adjustment.
- Redwood proposed kernel variant v2 for the serving runtime; early microbenchmarks promising but need production-ish tests.
- Next steps: targeted p95 microbench, traceroutes/BGP logs from customer, revised cost sheet, follow-up telemetry deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Live results review (p50/p95/error rates)
- Network routing and fallback behavior
- Kernel/serving runtime upgrade plan and canary windows
- Telemetry and observability ingestion into Splunk
- Pilot economics and egress options

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): okay everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, I think we have about 45 minutes, um, so quick intro — I'm Lena, AE on the account, Miguel's gonna drive the technical bits.
[00:12] Miguel (SE): hey all, hi, hello. we'll jump into the bench numbers and then the netops anomalies.
[00:18] Alex (CTO): sounds good, thanks. i've got Priya and Jordan on our side for the net and platform detail.
[00:25] Priya (NetOps): hi, thanks. quick note, we've also opened ticket NET-448 for the tracers.
[00:32] Miguel: great, ok first slide — current pilot baseline: p50 around 120ms, p95 spikes up to 980ms during our synthetic ramp tests in AZ-east-2, error rate stayed under 0.8% but we saw timeouts on batch joins.
[00:55] Jordan: sorry to interrupt — when you say timeouts on batch joins, is that client side or on the kernel side?
[01:00] Miguel: mostly upstream — the serving runtime dropped a few requests after KV cache misses coincided with elevated egress latencies. could be prefix cache warm-up interaction.
[01:15] Alex: hmm, we've been seeing packet fragmentation counters on the NIC for east-2 around the same time windows. MTU mismatch maybe?
[01:23] Priya: yep we flagged MTU earlier, but our infra team set it to 9000 across hosts, though the path to Redwood's egress gateway maybe stepping down.
[01:32] Miguel: ok that matches a theory — fragmentation increases CPU on the host and can amplify p95. we also suspect the egress shaping in the customer's firewall for that AZ is clipping bursts.
[01:45] Lena: can you explain the egress shaping bit again? some of our execs were concerned about predictable throughput vs cost, they're hearing "shaping" and think we're artificially limiting them.
[01:55] Miguel: sure — shaping is on the edge device (customer side) and it throttles sustained flows above X megabits, it's basically preventing short burst headroom. from Redwood's runtime viewpoint, that makes batching less effective, so per-token latency goes up. not Redwood throttling.
[02:18] Priya: just to note, our ops policy applies per-customer CIDR at the firewall, and there's a daytime throttle for heavy flows. we can relax it for the pilot but need a temporary exception.
[02:30] Lena: ok good, action item to Priya to share a temporary exception window, noted.
[02:36] Miguel: next, the kernel variant v2 — we ran a microbenchmark in staging with the v2 instruction path (optimized attention kernels) and saw p95 drop from 980 to ~260 under the same synthetic load, token throughput improved by about 18% in the harness.
[02:56] Alex: that's promising — is v2 compatible with our on-prem GPU drivers? we run a patched distro.
[03:04] Miguel: checked — v2 requires a minimum driver stack NVID-520, but it will fall back to v1 if missing. that fallback path is slightly slower. we do expect one minor dependency bump on kernel modules, which is why we want a short canary.
[03:20] Jordan: dependency bumps are fine, but we need a rollback plan; last time a driver upgrade caused a fragmentation of our container network plugin.
[03:28] Miguel: agreed — our rollback plan: 1) deploy v2 to canary pool with v1 fallback enabled, 2) run the same workload cymetrics for 2 hours, 3) if p95 regression > 10% or error rate > 1%, automatic rollback via orchestration, 4) keep snapshots of KV cache.
[03:51] Alex: how does the orchestration trigger the rollback? is it a webhook we manage or you?
[03:57] Lena: it's a joint play: Redwood sets the SLO thresholds and the orchestration triggers a rollout abort; customer can opt for manual override. we'll share the exact playbook.
[04:12] Priya: about telemetry — our Splunk ingestion missed ~12% of flow logs during last week's surge, likely due to sampling at the egress collector. can Redwood emit additional traces or flow metadata to a pull endpoint?
[04:25] Miguel: yes we can add an aggregated flow export to an S3 or push via HTTPS — but if Splunk's forwarder is dropping that, we might need to increase retention or reduce sampling. also the timestamps in our traces are sometimes recorded at different nodes, causing small misalignments.
[04:44] Jordan: we prefer Splunk HEC endpoint; can you provide a JSON schema for the flow payload so our SREs can validate before we bring it in?
[04:53] Miguel: sure, i'll send the schema and an example payload. will include low-cardinality tags: az, host-id, request-route.
[04:59] Alex: on routing — we observed two failovers where traffic flopped between primary and fallback regions, but the fallback route had 40ms extra hop causing increased p95. is there a way to adjust the fallback policy timing?
[05:12] Miguel: yes the routing policy is configurable — you can set the threshold for circuit breaker on RTT or success rate. for the pilot we recommend increasing the RTT threshold from 120ms to 200ms to avoid premature failover.
[05:25] Priya: let's test that in a canary window; our concern is that increasing threshold might mask real outages.
[05:31] Lena: agreed — we'll recommend a short canary: tweak threshold, run synthetic traffic for 1 hour, monitor error budgets.
[05:40] Miguel: quick note on KV cache warmups — Jordan suggested capturing point-in-time snapshots of the cache to reduce cold-starts. we can coordinate a warmup run immediately after deployment so first users don't see degradation.
[05:52] Jordan: yes we'll provide snapshot windows and coordinate with your deploy times.
[05:56] Alex: any security or compliance blockers? we need SOC 2 evidence and audit logs for the pilot to show to our compliance team.
[06:03] Lena: we have SOC 2 docs and an audit log export API. i'll attach the SOC 2 cert and the audit log sample in the follow-up email.
[06:12] Priya: also SSO — test SAML flow was fine but our IdP sessions timed out faster than Redwood's token TTL; small mismatch.
[06:20] Miguel: we can honor shorter session TTLs; not a technical blocker.
[06:24] Alex: ok great.
[06:27] Lena: wrapping up — recapping owners: Miguel runs p95 microbench with v2 by Tue 3/24, Priya provides traceroutes and BGP logs by Mon 3/23, Jordan confirms KV snapshot windows by Thu 3/26, Lena will send pilot cost/dedicated options and SOC 2 by Wed 3/25.
[06:45] Alex: thanks all, that schedule works for us.
[06:48] Miguel: one more micro point — during the microbench we noticed slightly higher CPU steal in one host; might be hypervisor timer config. we'll keep an eye on that.
[06:58] Priya: we'll surface the host telemetry, thanks.
[07:02] Lena: perfect, i'll follow up with calendar invite for the telemetry deep-dive and attach the cost sheet. thanks everyone.
[07:10] Alex: thanks, bye.

End of meeting.
